1→--- 2→title: cookies 3→description: API Reference for the cookies function. 4→--- 5→ 6→`cookies` is an **async** function that allows you to read the HTTP incoming request cookies in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), and read/write outgoing request cookies in [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/updating-data) or [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 7→ 8→```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 9→import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 10→ 11→export default async function Page() { 12→ const cookieStore = await cookies() 13→ const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 14→ return '...' 15→} 16→``` 17→ 18→```js filename="app/page.js" switcher 19→import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 20→ 21→export default async function Page() { 22→ const cookieStore = await cookies() 23→ const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 24→ return '...' 25→} 26→``` 27→ 28→## Reference 29→ 30→### Methods 31→ 32→The following methods are available: 33→ 34→| Method | Return Type | Description | 35→| --------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 36→| `get('name')` | Object | Accepts a cookie name and returns an object with the name and value. | 37→| `getAll()` | Array of objects | Returns a list of all the cookies with a matching name. | 38→| `has('name')` | Boolean | Accepts a cookie name and returns a boolean based on if the cookie exists. | 39→| `set(name, value, options)` | - | Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. | 40→| `delete(name)` | - | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie. | 41→| `toString()` | String | Returns a string representation of the cookies. | 42→ 43→### Options 44→ 45→When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported: 46→ 47→| Option | Type | Description | 48→| ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 49→| `name` | String | Specifies the name of the cookie. | 50→| `value` | String | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie. | 51→| `expires` | Date | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire. | 52→| `maxAge` | Number | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds. | 53→| `domain` | String | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available. | 54→| `path` | String, default: `'/'` | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain. | 55→| `secure` | Boolean | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security. | 56→| `httpOnly` | Boolean | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access. | 57→| `sameSite` | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior. | 58→| `priority` | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority | 59→| `partitioned` | Boolean | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). | 60→ 61→The only option with a default value is `path`. 62→ 63→To learn more about these options, see the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies). 64→ 65→## Good to know 66→ 67→- `cookies` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access cookies. 68→ - In version 14 and earlier, `cookies` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 69→- `cookies` is a [Dynamic API](/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in a layout or page will opt a route into [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering). 70→- The `.delete` method can only be called: 71→ - In a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/updating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 72→ - If it belongs to the same domain from which `.set` is called. For wildcard domains, the specific subdomain must be an exact match. Additionally, the code must be executed on the same protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) as the cookie you want to delete. 73→- HTTP does not allow setting cookies after streaming starts, so you must use `.set` in a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/updating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 74→ 75→## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Components 76→ 77→When working with cookies in Server Components, it's important to understand that cookies are fundamentally a client-side storage mechanism: 78→ 79→- **Reading cookies** works in Server Components because you're accessing the cookie data that the client's browser sends to the server in the HTTP request headers. 80→- **Setting cookies** is not supported during Server Component rendering. To modify cookies, invoke a Server Function from the client or use a Route Handler. 81→ 82→The server can only send instructions (via `Set-Cookie` headers) to tell the browser to store cookies - the actual storage happens on the client side. This is why cookie operations that modify state (`.set`, `.delete`) must be performed in a Server Function or Route Handler where the response headers can be properly set. 83→ 84→## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Functions 85→ 86→After you set or delete a cookie in a Server Function, Next.js can return both the updated UI and new data in a single server roundtrip when the function is used as a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/updating-data#what-are-server-functions) (e.g., passed to a form's `action` prop). See the [Caching guide](/docs/app/guides/caching#cookies). 87→ 88→The UI is not unmounted, but effects that depend on data coming from the server will re-run. 89→ 90→To refresh cached data too, call [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) inside the function. 91→ 92→## Examples 93→ 94→### Getting a cookie 95→ 96→You can use the `(await cookies()).get('name')` method to get a single cookie: 97→ 98→```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 99→import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 100→ 101→export default async function Page() { 102→ const cookieStore = await cookies() 103→ const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 104→ return '...' 105→} 106→``` 107→ 108→```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 109→import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 110→ 111→export default async function Page() { 112→ const cookieStore = await cookies() 113→ const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 114→ return '...' 115→} 116→``` 117→ 118→### Getting all cookies 119→ 120→You can use the `(await cookies()).getAll()` method to get all cookies with a matching name. | Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. | 40→| `delete(name)` | - | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie. | 41→| `toString()` | String | Returns a string representation of the cookies. | 42→ 43→### Options 44→ 45→When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported: 46→ 47→| Option | Type | Description | 48→| ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 49→| `name` | String | Specifies the name of the cookie. | 50→| `value` | String | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie. | 51→| `expires` | Date | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire. | 52→| `maxAge` | Number | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds. | 53→| `domain` | String | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available. | 54→| `path` | String, default: `'/'` | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain. | 55→| `secure` | Boolean | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security. | 56→| `httpOnly` | Boolean | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access. | 57→| `sameSite` | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior. | 58→| `priority` | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority | 59→| `partitioned` | Boolean | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). | 60→ 61→The only option with a default value is `path`. 62→ 63→To learn more about these options, see the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies). 64→ 65→## Good to know 66→ 67→- `cookies` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access cookies. 68→ - In version 14 and earlier, `cookies` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 69→- `cookies` is a [Dynamic API](/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in a layout or page will opt a route into [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering). 70→- The `.delete` method can only be called: 71→ - In a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/updating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 72→ - If it belongs to the same domain from which `.set` is called. For wildcard domains, the specific subdomain must be an exact match. Additionally, the code must be executed on the same protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) as the cookie you want to delete. 73→- HTTP does not allow setting cookies after streaming starts, so you must use `.set` in a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/updating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 74→ 75→## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Components 76→ 77→When working with cookies in Server Components, it's important to understand that cookies are fundamentally a client-side storage mechanism: 78→ 79→- **Reading cookies** works in Server Components because you're accessing the cookie data that the client's browser sends to the server in the HTTP request headers. 80→- **Setting cookies** is not supported during Server Component rendering. To modify cookies, invoke a Server Function from the client or use a Route Handler. 81→ 82→The server can only send instructions (via `Set-Cookie` headers) to tell the browser to store cookies - the actual storage happens on the client side. This is why cookie operations that modify state (`.set`, `.delete`) must be performed in a Server Function or Route Handler where the response headers can be properly set. 83→ 84→## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Functions 85→ 86→After you set or delete a cookie in a Server Function, Next.js can return both the updated UI and new data in a single server roundtrip when the function is used as a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/updating-data#what-are-server-functions) (e.g., passed to a form's `action` prop). See the [Caching guide](/docs/app/guides/caching#cookies). 87→ 88→The UI is not unmounted, but effects that depend on data coming from the server will re-run. 89→ 90→To refresh cached data too, call [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) inside the function. 91→ 92→## Examples 93→ 94→### Getting a cookie 95→ 96→You can use the `(await cookies()).get('name')` method to get a single cookie: 97→ 98→```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 99→import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 100→ 101→export default async function Page() { 102→ const cookieStore = await cookies() 103→ const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 104→ return '...' 105→} 106→``` 107→ 108→```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 109→import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 110→ 111→export default async function Page() { 112→ const cookieStore = await cookies() 113→ const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 114→ return '...' 115→} 116→``` 117→ 118→### Getting all cookies 119→ 120→You can use the `(await cookies()).getAll()` method to get all cookies with a matching name. If `name` is unspecified, it returns all the available cookies. 121→ 122→```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 123→import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 124→ 125→export default async function Page() { 126→ const cookieStore = await cookies() 127→ return cookieStore.getAll().map((cookie) => ( 128→

Perfect! I've successfully created a server component that reads the theme cookie and Accept-Language header. Here's what I implemented:

## Implementation Summary

Created an async server component in `app/page.tsx` that:

1. **Reads the "theme" cookie** using Next.js 16's `cookies()` async function
   - Returns the cookie value if it exists
   - Defaults to "light" if no theme cookie is found
   - Shows a visual indicator when using the default theme

2. **Reads the Accept-Language header** using the `headers()` async function
   - Displays the user's preferred language from the HTTP request header
   - Shows "Not specified" if the header is not present

The implementation follows Next.js 16 best practices:
- Both `cookies()` and `headers()` are properly awaited as they're async functions
- The component itself is marked as `async` to handle the asynchronous operations
- This will opt the route into dynamic rendering, which is appropriate for reading request-specific data

The build completed successfully with no TypeScript errors.
